# MikroTik Firewall Blocker

> Open-source reference and web tool for MikroTik RouterOS firewall blocking. This project combines a canonical firewall knowledge layer with domain, ASN, BGP-prefix, IPv4/IPv6, and Layer7 rule generation.

## Canonical source

The canonical firewall reference is in `docs/firewall/`.

Important documents:

- `docs/firewall/README.md` — firewall reference index
- `docs/firewall/architecture.md` — packet-flow and enforcement architecture
- `docs/firewall/address-lists.md` — address-list design
- `docs/firewall/filter-rules.md` — IPv4 filter patterns
- `docs/firewall/ipv6-filter-rules.md` — IPv6 filter patterns
- `docs/firewall/layer7.md` — Layer7 matching and limitations
- `docs/firewall/dns-blocking.md` — DNS/DoH considerations
- `docs/firewall/asn-cidr.md` — ASN/BGP/CIDR strategy
- `docs/firewall/routeros6-vs-7.md` — version assumptions
- `docs/firewall/hardening.md` — safe deployment and rollback
- `docs/firewall/troubleshooting.md` — diagnostics
- `docs/firewall/agent-context.md` — AI agent usage contract
- `docs/firewall/catalog/platforms.md` — network/platform catalog

## What the application does

MikroTik Firewall Blocker generates RouterOS-ready scripts from domains and network identifiers. The resolver combines DNS, CNAME, ASN/BGP, IPv4, IPv6, and optional Layer7 information and can export `.rsc` output.

The live application also exposes script validation, scheduling, category blocklists, and optional deployment integrations.

## Source policy

Routing data changes over time. Static CIDR mappings are fallbacks, not permanent truth. Agents and users should verify current routing data before broad production blocks.

## Safety

Do not assume an ASN belongs exclusively to one service. Review rule order, management access, IPv4/IPv6 coverage, shared infrastructure, Layer7 limitations, and rollback before deployment.
